prompts.text: What's a book, manuscript or written record that reveals something unexpected about a community's past?
Tell me about finding an old letter that made a historical period feel personal.
A local archive discovers a collection of handwritten notebooks. What information would help determine whose voices they preserve?
Preserving everyday writing can be as important as preserving official documents.
Reading a collection of family letters or exploring an early newspaper from your hometown?
Ordinary details in old documents can reveal the customs people rarely thought to explain.
Have you ever learned about a tradition through literature rather than seeing it practised?
You can create a small exhibition about one overlooked local writer. What would you want visitors to discover?
Describe encountering a story from another time that felt surprisingly connected to present life.
How can communities make historical records accessible without removing the context that gives them meaning?
What's a welcoming gesture you've encountered that made you feel at home in an unfamiliar place?
Tell me about visiting a household where the customs around receiving guests differed from your own.
You're hosting a visitor who doesn't know local dining etiquette. How would you make them comfortable without giving a lecture?
Hospitality is often expressed through small practical actions rather than elaborate ceremonies.
Learning about customary ways of offering refreshments or the traditions surrounding overnight guests?
A host's way of offering a seat or serving food can communicate a whole set of social expectations.
Have you noticed the meaning of bringing a gift change from one community to another?
Two friends disagree about whether it's polite to decline a second helping of food. What background might explain both views?
Describe a moment when someone explained their home's customs with warmth rather than embarrassment.
How do people balance their own hospitality traditions with a guest's personal boundaries?
Have you noticed communities organising daily life around very different ideas of punctuality or schedules?
Tell me about attending an event where the order of activities surprised you more than the start time.
An international team needs to plan a community gathering with several different scheduling customs. What might help avoid assumptions?
The way people organise time can reveal what a community values about relationships and obligations.
Learning about traditional seasonal calendars or exploring how weekly market days shaped local routines?
Some events are timed around natural conditions or social relationships rather than a fixed clock.
What traditional seasonal marker do people in your area still pay attention to?
A visitor asks why a festival happens at a different date each year. What would you want to know before answering?
Describe learning that an apparently casual meeting had an important local timing tradition.
How do modern work schedules affect celebrations that originally followed agricultural or seasonal cycles?
What's a cultural practice you first learned through play rather than being formally taught?
Tell me about a game, rhyme or story an older person taught you when you were young.
You want to introduce children to a traditional craft without turning it into a lecture. What activity could help?
Children often carry traditions forward by adapting them to the things they find enjoyable.
Learning through family storytelling or through taking part in community celebrations?
A child's questions can reveal assumptions adults have stopped noticing about their customs.
Have you ever seen a younger child ask about a tradition and receive several different explanations?
A school invites family members to share cultural skills. What would make the exchange respectful and engaging?
Describe discovering that a childhood activity was connected to a wider community tradition.
What should adults explain about a tradition before expecting children to participate?
Have you seen the same colour communicate different meanings at different celebrations?
Tell me about learning why a particular colour was important in a traditional garment or artwork.
You're documenting the colours used during a community festival. What would you ask people who choose the decorations?
Colour symbolism rarely has one universal meaning, even when the colours look familiar.
Exploring colour in ceremonial clothing or understanding the palette of traditional architecture?
The significance of a colour can depend on who is wearing it and what occasion it marks.
What's a colour combination that immediately reminds you of a place or cultural event?
A designer wants to use a cultural colour scheme for a public project. Whose perspective should they seek before proceeding?
Describe a time a colourful detail helped you recognise where a photograph had been taken.
How do colour traditions change when new fabrics and production methods become available?
What musical activity in your community brings people together beyond formal concerts?
Tell me about a song or rhythm that helped you understand a celebration's purpose.
A music researcher visits a community with a living singing tradition. What should they ask before recording anything?
The social role of music can be as important as its sound when understanding a tradition.
Learning the meaning of songs sung during work or exploring those performed at important life events?
Some songs exist mainly through participation, not through recordings that people listen to alone.
Have you noticed people changing a familiar traditional song to reflect something happening now?
A local choir wants to teach younger members songs known mostly by elders. How could the process respect both generations?
Describe a performance where you noticed the audience had an active role in the music.
How can people document communal music without separating it from the activities that give it meaning?
What's an object you've seen used on special occasions that would appear ordinary outside its context?
Tell me about learning why a familiar tool or vessel had a ceremonial role in one community.
A visitor sees an object at a cultural centre and wants to touch it. What information should the exhibit make clear?
Understanding how an object is used can matter more than knowing how old it is.
Studying household vessels that became symbolic or exploring objects made only for particular ceremonies?
A maker's technique can carry cultural significance even when the finished object seems simple.
Have you encountered an item whose meaning changed depending on who was permitted to use it?
A museum asks whether a private ceremonial object should remain on public display. Whose voices need to be part of the decision?
Describe a time an ordinary-looking item became interesting after someone explained its role.
What should visitors understand about the difference between viewing an object and participating in the practice around it?
How can a landscape hold cultural meaning beyond its natural appearance?
Tell me about visiting a place where somebody explained a story connected to a tree, hill or river.
You are helping document a local walking route with historical significance. Whose stories would you include?
Protecting a meaningful landscape can be part of preserving a community's cultural memory.
Exploring place-based oral histories or studying how old pathways connected settlements?
A familiar natural feature can be a landmark for generations even when it never appears in tourist guides.
What natural place do people in your area associate with a particular tradition or gathering?
A construction project could alter a culturally important public space. What questions should be asked before work begins?
Describe learning why a natural site mattered to people who lived near it.
How do communities communicate the importance of a landscape to newcomers who don't share its history?
What skill would you be interested in learning through a traditional apprenticeship?
Tell me about watching somebody pass a difficult craft technique to a younger person.
A craft workshop wants more apprentices but can't afford formal classes. What mentoring model could help?
A living craft survives through the relationships between makers as much as through the objects they create.
Spending a week learning pottery with a master maker or studying textile weaving alongside an experienced family?
Experienced craftspeople often recognise tiny mistakes that beginners wouldn't even notice.
What questions would you ask a maker about the parts of their skill that cannot easily be written down?
An apprentice wants to introduce modern tools into a traditional process. How could the teacher and learner test the idea together?
Describe a time someone gave you hands-on guidance that a written instruction couldn't provide.
How can communities encourage young people to take up traditional crafts as sustainable work?
What details in old celebration photographs reveal the era or place more clearly than the people's faces?
Tell me about seeing a family event photograph and discovering a tradition you'd never noticed before.
You are organising an old photo album of weddings and naming ceremonies. What questions would help create useful captions?
Family photographs can preserve cultural changes even when nobody intended them as historical records.
Comparing wedding fashions across generations or tracing how community celebrations changed venue over time?
The decorations, food and seating arrangements in an old photograph can tell their own story.
Have you ever been surprised by how formal or relaxed a family celebration looked decades ago?
An older relative recognises somebody in a photograph but not the occasion. What clues would you examine together?
Describe a conversation that began when someone pointed out a tiny detail in an old family picture.
What would you want a future family member to understand about the celebrations photographed today?
